title: TSMC Accelerates 1.4-Nanometer A14 Fab Buildout in Central Taiwan
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Taiwan has broken ground on an advanced packaging industrial park in Kaohsiung, reinforcing its ambition to remain at the center of the semiconductor industry as artificial intelligence drives demand for powerful chips.

The 88.7-hectare Baipu Industrial Park will devote 53.6 hectares to industrial use. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. plans to build two facilities there: a technology validation laboratory and a talent training center. Operations are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2029.

Unlike a conventional manufacturing expansion, Baipu is designed as a shared research and validation hub. Equipment and materials suppliers will be able to test technologies near TSMC’s advanced packaging operations, potentially shortening the journey from development to mass production. The arrangement could also help smaller Taiwanese companies qualify for participation in a demanding, growing supply chain.

Advanced packaging combines multiple chips or “chiplets” in a single system, improving performance while managing power use and manufacturing complexity. It has become essential for high-performance computing and AI processors designed by companies including Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. As demand accelerates, packaging capacity and technical expertise are emerging as strategic assets alongside leading-edge wafer fabrication.

President Lai Ching-te said the project would deepen Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem and strengthen southern Taiwan as a technology center. The park will complement TSMC’s nearby operations at the Nanzih Technology Industrial Park and broader packaging investments elsewhere in the south.

The project also highlights Taiwan’s effort to preserve the dense network of suppliers, engineers and research capabilities that underpins its chip leadership, even as TSMC expands overseas. Lai said the government would ensure stable electricity supplies through 2035, addressing a critical concern for energy-intensive semiconductor facilities.

By connecting research, supplier development and workforce training, Baipu aims to turn advanced packaging demand into durable industrial capacity and keep Taiwan indispensable to the next generation of computing.
